newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen rebounding, sentiment weak.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen rebounding, sentiment weak.

text.p: Stocks are expected to rebound on Tuesday, buoyed by the government's plan to encourage share buying by investment trusts, brokers said.
But they said an overhang of loans for margin trading and fears of a share oversupply would remain as a dampener.
"The government steps will boost the market today," said Lee Young-won, a broker at Daewoo Securities. "But the effect will be shortlived because of worsening fundamentals."
The finance ministry said on Monday it would allow three Seoul-based investment firms to raise capital by a combined 260 billion won to boost their share buying.
The composite stock index shed 2.05 percent, or 14.99 points, to end at a three-year low of 716.45 on Monday.
It was the lowest since October 9, 1993, when the index closed at 712.35.
The government's plan to sell 360 billion won worth of Korea Telecom shares this week and list the state-run company next year was a major factor dampening sentiment, they said.
